videos.script: Marginalia gets a steady stream of customer messages, and each one has to reach the right desk. {{tickets}} Shipping, returns, payments, accounts and e-books. Today a person reads every message and chooses. {{desks}} Lesson three used embeddings to find an article for a question. This lesson uses the same vectors to put a label on a message. {{label}} You will try four ways to do it. The first copies the label of the most similar message you have already sorted. {{neighbours}} The second compares the message with the average of each category. {{centroids}} The third trains a very small model on top of the vectors, in a fraction of a second. {{trained}} The fourth uses no examples at all, only a sentence describing each desk. {{zeroshot}} Then you will measure all four on fifty messages that none of them saw while learning. {{measure}} And you will read the ones they get wrong. Some of those mistakes belong to the method. Some belong to the label somebody chose. {{end}}
